title: 第2章 道观血案
content_zh:
第(1/3)页

“老人家好，我准备去城里逛逛。”见老人认出自己，阿丑也不觉得意外，走过去恭恭敬敬地回答。

他虽然很少出门，但“竹溪阿丑”这几个字早已传遍附近几个村落。

“去城里？”

老人盯着阿丑，哑然一笑道：“老头子听说，你弟弟要回家过年，你不会是被嫌弃赶出来了吧？”

阿丑没想到对方竟一下猜中要害，一时间不知如何作答。

老人叹了口气：“你也真是可怜，我要去鸡鸣山的道观送草料，那里山高路险，牛车上不去。

我年纪大了，一个人搬这一车草料着实不易，要不顺路带你一程，你帮我搬一下草料上山，你看能行吗？”

“没问题。”

阿丑闻言想了想，便答应下来。

随后坐上牛车，朝鸡鸣山方向走去，路上听着老人一路唠叨，原本压抑的心情也舒缓了一些。

牛车拉着重物，行走速度并不快，足足走了一个多时辰，才终于来到一座覆着积雪的石山脚下。

老人跳下车，抬头望了一眼山顶，转身对阿丑说：“鸡鸣山到了，麻烦你帮我搬一下草料吧。”

“好。”

阿丑跟着下来，扛起两大捆草料，就朝山上走去。

山路蜿蜒崎岖，寻常人走路都费劲，好在阿丑平日干惯了农活，虽然有些吃力，但还可以承受得住。

倒是后面的老人，哪怕只扛一捆草料，也累得上气不接下气，走不了多久就要停下休息。

“你小子倒是干活的好手，要不是面貌有些惊人，我都想把孙女许配给你了。”

老人从后面跟上来，感慨地说道。

阿丑闻言只是笑笑，便埋着头继续向上走去。

山顶上有一座道观，名叫鸡鸣观。

当阿丑和农家老人来到观门口时，却发现大门紧闭着，老人上前拍了好几下，里面都没有半点回应。

“怎么回事，不是约好今天送草料的吗，怎么没人开门？”老人嘴里抱怨着，手上的力道也加重了几分。

当老人准备拍第三下的时候，大门忽然从里面拉开了。

一个身穿血色衣袍，长着两只尖尖耳朵的老人，站在门后冷冷地盯着两人。

不知是山顶风大还是怎么的，阿丑忽然感觉，周围空气似乎变得冰冷了几分。

“你们是谁。”

血袍老人沙哑着开口，两只眼睛微微眯起。

content_en:
Page (1/3)

"Hello, old man, I'm going to go for a walk in the city." Seeing that the old man recognized him, A Chou was not surprised, so he walked over and answered respectfully.

Although he rarely goes out, the words "Zhuxi A Chou" have already spread to several nearby villages.

"Going to the city?"

The old man stared at A Chou and said with a dumb smile: "Old man, I heard that your brother is going home for the New Year. Are you being kicked out because of disgust?"

A Chou didn't expect that the other party would guess the key point at once, and he didn't know how to answer for a while.

The old man sighed: "You are really pitiful. I want to deliver fodder to the Taoist temple in Jiming Mountain. The mountains are high and the roads are dangerous, and the oxcart cannot go there."

I'm old, and it's not easy for me to carry this cart of hay by myself. How about I give you a ride along the way? You can help me carry the hay up the mountain. Do you think it's possible?"

"No problem."

A scandalyan thought about it and agreed.

Then I got on the bullock cart and walked towards Jiming Mountain. Listening to the old man chattering along the way, my originally depressed mood relaxed a little.

The bullock cart was pulling heavy loads and the walking speed was not very fast. After walking for more than an hour, we finally arrived at the foot of a snow-covered stone mountain.

The old man jumped out of the car, looked up at the top of the mountain, turned to A Chou and said, "We've arrived at Jiming Mountain. Please help me move the fodder."

"Okay."

A Chou followed down, picked up two large bundles of fodder, and walked towards the mountain.

The mountain road was winding and rugged, making it difficult for ordinary people to walk. Fortunately, A Chou was used to farm work, so although it was a bit strenuous, he could still bear it.

On the other hand, the old man behind him was so tired that he was out of breath even if he was only carrying a bundle of hay. He would have to stop and rest after walking for a long time.

"You are really good at work. If it weren't for your amazing appearance, I would have betrothed my granddaughter to you."

The old man followed up from behind and said with emotion.

Ah Changyan just smiled and continued walking up with his head buried.

There is a Taoist temple on the top of the mountain called Jiming Temple.

When A Chou and the old farmer came to the gate, they found that the door was tightly closed. The old man stepped forward and patted it several times, but there was no response at all.

"What's going on? Didn't we make an appointment to deliver fodder today? Why is no one opening the door?" the old man complained, and the strength in his hands became a little stronger.

When the old man was about to take the third shot, the door suddenly opened from the inside.

An old man wearing a blood-colored robe with two pointed ears stood behind the door and stared at the two of them coldly.

I don't know whether it was because of the strong wind on the top of the mountain or something else, but A Chou suddenly felt that the air around him seemed to have become a bit colder.

"Who are you?"

The old man in blood robe spoke hoarsely, his eyes slightly narrowed.
